exact_arguments.prompt:
Create a new authored HAVENLINE GRADE-SEPARATED CONVEYOR CROSSING concept sheet, exactly 1536 by 1024 pixels. Four equal panels on the established peach studio floor, same polished stylized game-render language. This crossing is an additional module in the already approved transport family. The first reference is the approved straight/corner/height-adapter kit: preserve its orange closed side housings, yellow top rails, closely spaced round dark transverse cylinders, flat silver end/bridge plates with small round bolts and thin blue lower trim. The second reference reinforces the approved original conveyor styling and C1 identity. The third reference defines the approved fish sizes: use ONLY its largest blue-gray SALMON, with dark blue fins and tail, as the load on BOTH independent routes; its whole-body length is approximately half the human C1 height. Preserve that load-to-human relationship. Do not substitute tiny fish or shrink the load at the underpass.

The SAME ONE crossing design must appear in all views. It consists of TWO CONTINUOUS INDEPENDENT loaded conveyor routes at right angles, physically separated in height. The lower route is one straight, level, low conveyor all the way through the crossing. The upper route begins low, climbs a long GENTLE supported ramp, has a clearly FLAT horizontal bridge span over the lower route, then descends by a matching long gentle supported ramp back to low height. Both upper approach and departure and both lower approach and departure must be unambiguous. The paths do not join, transfer cargo, intersect at a common level or share rollers.

The upper bridge must have an actual open cargo passage underneath. Its underside must be well ABOVE the highest dorsal fin of a largest approved salmon riding the lower conveyor, with a generous visible stripe of empty air between fish and underside. Show a salmon genuinely occupying this lower passage while another salmon occupies the upper bridge; their solid bodies, fins and tails never touch or overlap either route, rails, support, plate or other cargo. Use realistic spacing: isolated whole fish, no piles. Across the sheet, loads on the lower route retain the same large approved size as those on the upper route. All salmon lie lengthwise along their own direction of travel and remain entirely inside the useful lane width. Silver bridge/transition plates are flat and flush, not blocking walls.

Keep the physical form compact and low in this family. Use continuous orange ramp side cheeks with blue low bases and compact paired side abutments beside the lower route. No support may occupy the lower lane or its fish-clearance envelope. Only the short crossing span bridges the open passage. The long rise and fall are properly supported to the floor. The bridge top remains around C1 waist height, only high enough to clear the full lower housing and its large salmon. Ordinary approaches remain below the knee like the approved kit. Avoid tall stilt factory frames, generic tall motors, scaffolding, ladders, stairs, towering bridge arches or exaggerated vertical cliffs. Ramps are long and gentle, never abrupt steep wedges or unsupported floating conveyors. This new crossing has no exact 13-roller requirement; use consistently close transverse round rollers appropriate to each continuous segment.

PANEL TOP LEFT, label TOP OBLIQUE: a clear full front three-quarter view of the entire crossing. Show the long upper rise, flat bridge, supported fall, and the straight lower route visible entering and leaving at ninety degrees. Several well-spaced large salmon demonstrate both complete independent routes. One unchanged full C1 stands on the peach floor to the side of the machine for scale, never on a belt.

PANEL TOP RIGHT, label REVERSE OBLIQUE: the exact same crossing from the opposite corner, with the same structure, support positions, routing, proportions, colors and fish scale. Make the lower exit and the far side of the bridge visible. One unchanged complete C1 beside it at the same physical scale. This is the reverse camera, not a redesigned crossing.

PANEL BOTTOM LEFT, label SIDE CLEARANCE: a low side view focused on the crossing opening with its orange side supports. Make the vertical empty gap between a complete large lower-lane salmon's tallest fin and the upper bridge underside plainly visible. Also show a full large salmon resting on the upper bridge above it. Let enough upper rise and fall remain visible to prove the level bridge and proper support. The lane separation must be readable from actual geometry and empty air, with no cutaway, transparency or fake clearance diagram. Keep a full unchanged C1 on the adjacent floor at the same physical scale. Never crop C1's head or boots.

PANEL BOTTOM RIGHT, label WALKWAY AROUND: show this crossing installed as the same compact machine. The pedestrian route is a wide, unobstructed peach-floor path around the OUTSIDE of the entire conveyor footprint and its ramp ends, leading to an open wooden camp gate beyond it. The path does not pass through the lower cargo opening, under the crossing, across a live belt, or between touching loads. One complete unchanged C1 stands on this outside walkway, safely clear of cargo. Keep the open gate and access clear; no machine or conveyor blocks the gate. Both fish routes remain independent and loaded.

C1 is the exact established brown-skinned male with short curly black hair, glasses, beard, navy winter jacket with orange trim and pale fleece hood/cuffs, navy trousers and brown boots. Keep his anatomy, outfit, proportions and human-relative machine scale fixed across views; one full human per panel. Maintain the same peach background, soft light and ground shadows throughout. Labels are only the four specified short panel titles. No measurement text, gameplay HUD, recipe claims, controls or runtime claims. This is a newly authored crossing design study, not purported video footage. Deliver the actual four-view render sheet.

scope: New authored crossing study; no reference-video exact-match or runtime approval.
